nodes.summary: There exist finite groups $G$ and $H$ such that $G$ is almost simple, $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type, and $G$ is not isomorphic to $H$. That is, the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 21.134(b) is false.
nodes.title: Power-equation type does not characterize almost simple groups

nodes.summary: The conjecture that for all finite groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is almost simple and $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type, then $G$ is isomorphic to $H$.
nodes.title: Characterization of almost simple groups by power-equation type (Kourovka 21.134(b))

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is almost simple when there is a nonabelian finite simple group $S$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup $A$ of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ that contains the inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S)$.
nodes.title: Almost simple group

nodes.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type when, for every positive integer $n$, the equation $x^n = 1$ has the same number of solutions in $G$ as in $H$. An infinite set of solutions is counted as $0$, so the notion is meant for finite groups.
nodes.title: Same power-equation type

nodes.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the same type when, for every integer $n \ge 1$, the equation $x^n = 1$ has the same number of solutions in $G$ as in $H$, where an infinite set of solutions counts as having $0$ elements.
nodes.title: Groups of the same type

nodes.summary: The answer to Kourovka Problem 12.37 is negative: there are finite groups $G$ and $H$ of the same type such that $H$ is soluble and $G$ is not soluble.
nodes.title: Solubility is not determined by the type

nodes.summary: Every finite group of the same type as a finite soluble group is soluble: if $G$ and $H$ are finite groups of the same type and $H$ is soluble, then $G$ is soluble.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.37 (J. G. Thompson)
